key_insight: A unified compressible unsteady-aerofoil theory shows that surface permeability strongly alters gust and heave loading, and that porous-to-impermeable load reduction cannot be predicted by simply mixing incompressible porous and compressible rigid models.
engineering_relevance: For porous aerofoil and flow-control design, permeability must be modeled together with compressibility and unsteady wake effects to avoid large errors in predicted load alleviation.
method: Combines Possio’s integral operator with a convective permeable boundary condition for finite-chord aerofoils.
Allows chordwise-varying admittance while retaining wake dynamics and the unsteady Kutta condition.
Uses weighted-Jacobi collocation; edge and discontinuity exponents remain in incompressible form in terms of local permeability.
evidence_signal: The formulation is verified against published incompressible results and an independent compressible theory, and the abstract reports large discrepancies with mixed-theory estimates—up to about a factor of two, and 1.4 to 4.3 in some Mach/frequency ranges.
watch_item: Do not estimate porous load reduction by combining separate incompressible-porous and compressible-rigid theories; the error can remain significant even at low Mach numbers and depends on compactness (Mach number × reduced frequency).
paper_title: Compressible unsteady aerodynamics of finite-chord porous aerofoils
